instruction: Triage my inbox. It's overflowing, so give me a per-sender count and the top 10 senders filling it up.
required_subtasks: Grep Maildir folders (including ~/Maildir/cur/, ~/Maildir/new/, and sub-folders like .Work/, .Travel/, .Receipts/ with their cur/ and new/) for From: headers excluding michael.scott@dundermifflin.com
Group by sender email address
Count messages per sender
Rank top 10 senders
Report the top-10 list with counts

rubrics.criterion: Agent reads Michael's HooliMail inbox messages — via the HooliMail app/API listing the Inbox folder including any sub-folders (Work, Travel, Receipts, etc.), OR by walking the Maildir filesystem at ~/Maildir/cur, ~/Maildir/new, and sub-folder cur/new dirs — but excludes the Sent folder and excludes Michael's own From: lines when counting senders
Agent groups the inbox messages by sender email and counts how many messages each sender is filling it up with
Agent reports the inbox senders as a top-10 ranked list with per-sender counts
Agent presents the top-10 inbox senders as a readable ranked list with one sender per line and a visible count column
Agent lists approximately 10 inbox sender entries in the top-senders ranking (not just 5 or 7)

instruction: Compose a quick new email to Pam in HooliMail with my signature ('World's Best Boss, Somehow I Manage') typed at the bottom of the body. Save it as a draft so I can review and send later.
required_subtasks: Open HooliMail
Click Write to compose a new email
Address To: pam.beesly@dundermifflin.com (HooliMail seeds Pam's contact at this address)
Add a one-line subject (e.g. 'Quick note')
Type a short message body
Add a 'World's Best Boss, Somehow I Manage' signature line at the end of the body
Save as draft (do not send)

rubrics.criterion: Agent opens HooliMail and clicks Write to open a new compose window addressed to pam.beesly@dundermifflin.com
Agent fills a non-empty subject line (e.g. 'Quick note') in the HooliMail compose window
Agent writes a short message body in the new HooliMail draft to Pam
Agent appends the 'World's Best Boss, Somehow I Manage' signature line at the end of the email body before saving
Agent saves the email to Pam as a draft in HooliMail (does not hit Send) so Michael can review later
Agent's draft persists in the HooliMail Drafts folder after saving and the signature line is visible in the saved draft body

instruction: Help me auto-triage my inbox. Which senders do I usually reply to fast, and which ones do I let sit for days? I want to build a priority filter around that pattern.
required_subtasks: List Michael's top sent-mail recipients — either by walking ~/Maildir/.Sent/ on the filesystem (grep '^From: michael.scott' recursively) or by listing the HooliMail Sent folder via /api/emails?folder=sent (both surface the same 80+ sent emails)
For each recipient, pair received timestamps with Michael's reply timestamps in the same thread
Compute a rough 'median reply latency' per top recipient
Identify which ~3 senders get his fastest replies and which get the slowest / none
Recommend an auto-triage priority rule based on the observed pattern

rubrics.criterion: Agent locates Michael's sent emails to build the auto-triage data set — either by walking the Maildir filesystem (.Sent/cur or .Sent/new with 'From: michael.scott' grep) or by querying the HooliMail Sent folder via /api/emails?folder=sent
Agent computes a median reply latency per top sender from the paired received/sent timestamps and surfaces which senders Michael lets sit for days
Agent identifies the fastest-reply and slowest-reply senders with supporting evidence
Agent proposes a concrete auto-triage filter rule based on the data
Agent derives the fast-vs-days reply pattern from Maildir timestamps rather than guessing, and names Michael as the sender of record
Agent finishes the auto-triage build: the recommended priority filter rule is stated and references the fastest and slowest senders

instruction: Start a draft email to David Wallace with my most recent quarter's sales summary. Pull a ballpark from my ~/Downloads/DunderMifflin_Q2_Sales_Forecast.txt so the numbers actually have a basis. Save it as a draft; do NOT hit send. I want to review it first. Do some analysis in LibreOffice Calc so I have some empirical analysis to send him as well.
required_subtasks: Open Files and read ~/Downloads/DunderMifflin_Q2_Sales_Forecast.txt for sales figures
Open LibreOffice Calc and perform sales analysis using figures from the forecast file
Open HooliMail and start a new message
Address it to david.wallace@dundermifflin.com
Summarize the most recent quarter's sales in the body (numbers grounded in the forecast doc)
Save as draft without sending

rubrics.criterion: Agent reads ~/Downloads/DunderMifflin_Q2_Sales_Forecast.txt to extract the sales figures that ground the email body

Agent performs sales analysis in LibreOffice Calc using figures from the forecast file, producing a spreadsheet with empirical analysis (totals, trends, or comparisons) as an attachment or saved file for Michael to send along
Agent saves the most-recent-quarter sales summary email to David Wallace as a HooliMail draft and does not send it, so Michael can review it first
Draft is addressed to david.wallace@dundermifflin.com and the body references the most recent quarter's sales grounded in figures from the forecast file
Agent explicitly notes that it did not hit Send, leaving the HooliMail draft for Michael to review before sending

date_policy_notes: Instruction references the bake-time filename ~/Downloads/DunderMifflin_Q2_Sales_Forecast.txt directly so the task does not depend on the boot-time rename patcher. 'Most recent quarter' stays a relative phrase regardless of the Q2 tag in the filename.
